CONFOUND: Strained molecules are +4.0 heavy atoms larger (p=0.0402). SA rises with size independently of ring strain, so the SA effect is NOT cleanly attributable to strain alone at n=25/group. The N=200 checkpoint sweep must report SA conditional on BOTH strain and heavy-atom count, or the attribution stays ambiguous.
COUNTERFACTUAL: The strained-free subgroup scores quality 0.40 against the GuacaMol corpus reference 0.4236, i.e. near corpus parity. This is an ASSOCIATION within one sample of 50, NOT a proven causal counterfactual: it assumes removing the defect leaves the rest of the generative process unchanged. It motivates the checkpoint sweep; it does not substitute for it.
POWER: n=25 per group. Adequate for the SA effect; QED and heavy-atom effects are weaker and need the N=200 sweep.
READING: Strained-ring molecules are worse on BOTH axes, not SA alone. SA is the larger effect (+0.946 mean, permutation p=0.0034); QED is also worse (-0.120, p=0.0173); strained molecules are also larger (+4.0 heavy atoms, p=0.0402). The earlier claim that 'the ENTIRE gap is SA' is therefore TOO STRONG and is corrected here: the small-ring defect degrades SA primarily and QED secondarily, and is confounded with molecule size.
